newsitem.title: USA: Mostly clear weather should aid US Midwest harvest.
newsitem.headline: Mostly clear weather should aid US Midwest harvest.

text.p: Except for a few light showers Monday and Wednesday in the U.S. Midwest, farmers should have favorable harvest weather this week, U.S. meteorologists said.
"There shouldn't be any major harvest problems this week," said Joel Burgio, agricultural meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.

Rain measuring 0.10 to 0.40 inch fell in eastern Nebraska and southwest and central Iowa since late Sunday. The showers should move east with less than 0.50 inch likely Monday in eastern Iowa, northwest Illinois and southern Wisconsin.

Another shower system was forecast to enter the Midwest Wednesday, with 0.25 to 0.75 inch of rain likely over 50 percent of the area. After Wednesday, clear weather is forecast with normal to above normal temperatures, said Craig Solberg, Freese-Notis meteorologist.
"Basically, beyond early Thursday we are shifting into a favorable harvest weather pattern," said Solberg.
Solberg said the rain forecast for Wednesday should cause brief harvest delays.
"I would not be surprised at all to see some farmers, with well-drained fields, to be at work Thursday," he said.
Although cold, much of this past weekend was dry allowing for rapid harvesting, grain dealers said. Some dealers said much of the soybean harvest could be completed this week.
"It looks like there are two or three decent days ahead. They should finish the beans up," said an Indiana dealer.
The Midwest should feature normal to above normal temperatures until the weekend, when below-normal temperatures were forecast to return to the region, meteorologists said.

The High Plains also should be dry this week except for a few light showers Monday and Wednesday in eastern areas. Temperatures should fluctuate from normal Monday, above normal Tuesday, below normal Thursday and back to above normal Saturday, said WSC's Burgio.
